results.content:
Pttrns is a foundational resource for sourcing inspirational app design, functioning as a curated gallery of mobile UI patterns. Its long standing reputation is built on a simple premise: providing thousands of categorized screenshots from real iOS and Android apps, allowing designers to quickly find solutions for specific user interface challenges. Unlike platforms focused on broad design assets, Pttrns hones in on mobile specific patterns, making it a fast and efficient tool for ideation. [...] For teams crafting compelling app store visuals, Pttrns offers a rapid way to benchmark against established design conventions. By browsing categories relevant to your app, you can quickly identify the visual language and interaction patterns that users already understand and expect. This insight is crucial for designing app store screenshots that feel both innovative and intuitive, reducing friction and boosting conversion rates. [...] > Actionable Takeaway: When designing a new feature, search Pttrns for similar UI flows such as "Subscription" or "Search". Analyze the top examples to identify common layouts. Use an app store screenshot editor to apply these established patterns to your designs, ensuring your feature’s value is communicated instantly and effectively.

results.title: App Store Screenshot Best Practices: 5 Rules That Convert
results.content:
Five fundamentals drive App Store screenshot conversion in 2026: lead with the outcome on the first frame, wrap your real app UI in a current device frame, keep typography readable at thumbnail size, maintain visual consistency across the full set, and respect the platform split (iOS rewards lifestyle, Android rewards feature clarity). Apple's App Store Review Guidelines require actual in-app UI in screenshots ( so the design work happens around your screens, not in place of them.

TL;DR: [...] Apple doesn't publish a numeric split, but a widely-used community heuristic is 60/40: aim for at least 60% of frames showing real app UI and no more than 40% pure lifestyle or marketing. The underlying constraint is real, since sets that are mostly marketing art with little visible UI tend to get rejected under Apple's accuracy guidelines ( Plan the set so at least 6 of 10 frames feature real screens.

## What are the App Store screenshot design trends in 2026? [...] Showing iPhone 14 frames in 2026 signals an unmaintained app. The current standard frames developers should use:

 iPhone 16 Pro Max (6.9-inch, 1320×2868)
 iPad Pro 13-inch (2064×2752) if you support iPad
 Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra for Play Store
 Pixel 9 Pro for Play Store as alternative
